purpose: Install headroom-ai==0.38.0 (mcp extra) into a NEW isolated uv-tool prefix alongside the pinned 0.37.0, read its actual CLI/MCP docs, and run the same guarded MCP compress/retrieve recovery check the 0.37.0 receipt ran, to settle whether the pin_behind_upstream flag on token-efficiency gap 2 is safe to advance.
preregistered: If headroom_compress+headroom_retrieve on 0.38.0 returns byte-for-byte original content (sha256 match) for the owned fixtures/rag-note.md artifact and the CLI help confirms the critic's correction (no `headroom compress` CLI subcommand, MCP-only path), the pin_behind_upstream flag can advance from 0.37.0 to 0.38.0 as a safe upgrade candidate; if recovery is inexact, or the MCP tool errors, or a compress CLI subcommand now exists contradicting the correction, the pin stays at 0.37.0 and the discrepancy is recorded honestly. This check does not exercise the proxy-intercept path (proxy target 127.0.0.1:1 is intentionally unreachable, matching the 0.37.0 receipt's own fixture) and does not touch the live 0.37.0 install or its ledger.

commands.cmd: UV_TOOL_DIR=<new-prefix>/uv-tool-dir UV_TOOL_BIN_DIR=<new-prefix>/bin UV_PYTHON=.../python3.13 uv tool install --python 3.13 'headroom-ai[mcp]==0.38.0'

commands.output_excerpt: no `compress` top-level command listed; commands are audit-reads, evals, inspect, mcp, savings (each description mentions 'compression' but there is no bare `compress` verb)
MCP server for Claude Code integration... tools are named headroom_retrieve / headroom_compress / etc. ... Commands: install, reconcile, serve, status, uninstall

commands.cmd: mcporter call --stdio <new-prefix>/bin/headroom --stdio-arg mcp --stdio-arg serve --stdio-arg --proxy-url --stdio-arg http://127.0.0.1:1 --name headroom038check --tool headroom_compress --args '{"content": "<fixtures/rag-note.md, 351 bytes>"}' --output json --no-oauth

mcporter call --stdio <new-prefix>/bin/headroom --stdio-arg mcp --stdio-arg serve --stdio-arg --proxy-url --stdio-arg http://127.0.0.1:1 --name headroom038check --tool headroom_retrieve --args '{"hash":"27680cf43a65121fc1affbde"}' --output json --no-oauth

mcporter call --stdio <new-prefix>/bin/headroom --stdio-arg mcp --stdio-arg serve --stdio-arg --proxy-url --stdio-arg http://127.0.0.1:1 --name headroom038check --tool headroom_stats --args '{}' --output json --no-oauth

result: 0.38.0 CLI help confirms the critic's correction: there is no `headroom compress` CLI subcommand (only audit-reads/evals/inspect/mcp/savings, each of which mentions compression in its description but none is a bare `compress` verb); the MCP path (`headroom mcp serve`, tools headroom_compress/headroom_retrieve/headroom_stats) is unchanged in shape from 0.37.0. A live MCP session on the new 0.38.0 binary compressed the owned fixtures/rag-note.md (351 bytes / 75 tokens) with transform 'router:noop' (no reduction for this small artifact) and headroom_retrieve returned content that matched the original byte-for-byte (sha256 27680cf43a65121fc1affbde0dba8021ea21180bb8db0a9c0f80a09b831257cc on both sides; headroom's own content hash 27680cf43a65121fc1affbde is confirmed to be the first 24 hex chars of that same sha256). The configured proxy at 127.0.0.1:1 was reported unreachable exactly as in the 0.37.0 receipt's fixture, so the proxy-intercept path itself was not exercised by either version's receipt. The pinned 0.37.0 install was not modified.

verdict_impact.explanation: Exact MCP compress/retrieve recovery holds on 0.38.0 for this owned fixture and the CLI-surface shape (no compress subcommand) matches the critic's correction, so nothing here blocks advancing the pin_behind_upstream flag from 0.37.0 to 0.38.0. It only partially settles gap 2 because this run used one small, low-entropy fixture (351 bytes, noop transform triggered) rather than the larger MCP-tool-listing fixture that produced the 0.37.0 receipt's 36,625-vs-19,714-token compression numbers, so compression-ratio behavior on 0.38.0 (as opposed to exact-recovery correctness) is not yet independently confirmed at that scale.

limitations: Fixture is small (351 bytes / 75 tokens) and triggered a no-op transform, so this run demonstrates exact recovery but not a compression-ratio comparison against the 0.37.0 receipt's larger fixture.
The configured Headroom proxy (127.0.0.1:1) was unreachable by design in both the 0.37.0 and 0.38.0 fixtures, so automatic proxy-intercept compression was not exercised by either receipt.
Only one MCP round-trip (compress+retrieve+stats) was run once as preregistered; no retry or alternate-fixture rerun was performed.
Individual MCP call durations were not precisely instrumented (each completed well under its 60s command timeout); duration_s values for those three commands are approximate.

The installed wheel's sha256 was not independently recomputed from the local uv cache; it is recorded from PyPI's published JSON API digest for the matching platform tag, which the installer would have verified against at download time.
